(1) stress increases glutamatergic neurotransmission in the hippocampus, which (2) causes a decrease in hippocampal GABA, which (3) leads to a decrease in the inhibitory control of the prefrontal cortex (PFC) and (4) results in a hyperactive PFC that is unable to properly regulate hippocampal activity.

(1) in individuals at risk for psychosis, glutamate levels in the hippocampus are elevated, (2) the elevated glutamate in the hippocampus causes psychosis, and (3) this effect of glutamate is mediated by the NMDA receptor.
